report.methodologyNote: Heuristic score based on weighted class contributions. This is not an official regulatory index — see note below.
report.methodologyContent:
This score is a heuristic weighted index — not an official regulatory metric. No universal standard exists for mapping satellite semantic segmentation labels to a single pollution score. The approach is inspired by:

  • EU Marine Strategy Framework Directive (MSFD) — Descriptors 8, 9, 10 for contaminants, eutrophication, and marine litter
  • NOAA Marine Debris Program — standardized debris monitoring protocols
  • Water Quality Index (CCME WQI) — weighted aggregation methodology

Each class is assigned a pollution weight (0-10) based on its association with anthropogenic activity or ecosystem stress. The final index = weighted sum of pixel percentages, normalized to 0-10.

pollution.descClean: Water body appears clean with minimal anthropogenic influence.
pollution.descLight: Slight presence of potential pollutants detected; natural conditions largely dominant.
pollution.descModerate: Moderate pollution indicators suggest human activity or algal presence affecting water quality.
pollution.descHeavy: Significant pollution signals — oil, debris, or industrial presence likely.
pollution.descSevere: Severe pollution detected. Strong presence of oil spills, marine debris, or industrial activity.
